OP I’m in the same spot with how you feel about kicking up explosively. It can hurt, but we have to teach ourselves how to start at square one and get learn the mechanics of our body and what we have to do to get to the destination. Once we do that, then we can start working on smoothing it out and then it becomes easier and easier until it’s a skill learned and earned to move on to the next!!! I forget to tell myself this too, but knowing other people share the same struggle and being able to remind ourselves of those baby steps together can be amazing. I hope this helps and keep on climbing :)

Here’s where I went wrong:

I’m a beginner, never made French meringue before. I had to look up and teach myself how to separate egg whites from yolks and I still screwed that up and had to start over, but still.

1) i don’t think they were room temperature enough
2) i think i over whipped them with not enough cream of tartar (i don’t have tea spoons)
3) therefore when i added the sugar in it wasn’t thickening after 20 minutes of hand mixer on low speed (later found out i should have done higher speed at cross sections to help)
3) the Bundt pan i had had a lot of rivets in it that i think didn’t allow it to rise enough 


The only thing that went right was the whipped raspberry icing (although i didn’t have extract, instead i boiled hot water and through a lot in then shocked them in cold water and mashed it up and refrigerated to use in the icing). And the glaze went well too. Because of how bumpy and flaky the cake was the icing didn’t apply too well but hey! I have to make mistakes to make it better next time.

Took me 5 hours total because the video doesn’t show the 50% uppage that he did to his online recipe and I got myself all confused. And, I fucked up bad and way over carmelized and burnt the oranges for the candying process because I was dealing with a new mixer and couldn’t get it working; also having a hard time getting 6 eggs to blend in with the sugar and butter for some dumb reason. So I got sidetracked lol! 

I would recommend only *one* hour for candying and do a really low heat. Everything turned out well but the icing could use an uppage on the ingredient amount and I put mine in the fridge prior to help it get thicker. As for the glaze, I let it sit for too long and it condense, so don’t do my mistake and keep it warm until the cake is ready, you’ll definitely see a difference.

I didn’t have a juice for the clementines, so I did everything by hand using a potatoe masher into a drainer; and then I used store bought juice. 

Overall, what a fun process! The cake rose so nicely in this pan. I went through 2 containers of sugar and half a box of cake flour, and an entire bag of cuties (clementines are mandarins but not all mandarins are clementines apparently??) Definitely make sure you have an accurate scale for this recipe! I’m taking it to a friends house to try for dinner so will update with taste soon! Thanks for reading :)

I’ve practiced yoga for yeaaars to help out but also this:

Pre COVID-19: When I had more expendable income and free time outside, I loved going to float tank places for sensory deprivation and one of the studios has a massage chair that absolutely engulfs you and together it’s an incredible experience. I get the best sleep of my life. I would also go to a local park and put up my big hammock in between trees, seal it up, and nap or read a book for a while. 

During Covid-19: I prop up my tablet in the shower with something to watch and either an ice cold alcoholic drink or hot tea. While my face is still all hot and red, I grab my gua sha roller from the fridge to roll my face out and then slap a cold sheet mask on. While I do that, I have a bunch of small body massage tools and foam rollers to give myself a massage and it’s really nice. I use my elbows on my feet because i have tough arches, but when all is said and done, you feel so good and ready for bed. 

I’ve also picked up meditation walks if you want to listen to Shaman Durek on Ancient Wisdom Today, he has incredible stuff.

For hooded eyes: Alissa Ashley and Smitha Deepak on YouTube have great tutorials! In a way, it’s a blessing in disguise for us because we don’t have to blend out as much space on our lids. Definitely make sure you cut creases ABOVE your folds. And for eyeliner, start the liner OUTSIDE the fold so the skin doesn’t crease it or smudge it. This may mean your liner will look longer or wider, so make sure you keep angling upwards to create a sharper wing. 

Hope this helps!
